cumleler: In continuous vertigo, why is a normal head impulse not good news?
HINTS is an eye exam: head impulse, nystagmus, and test of skew.
In vestibular neuritis, impulses toward the affected side show a corrective saccade.
In most cerebellar or brainstem strokes, however, the VOR pathway is spared.
So in acute continuous vertigo, a normal impulse suggests a central cause.
Even one central sign calls for prompt emergency physician evaluation.
